macro.text: Nasdaq futures surge as investors pile back into battered AI stocks: Nasdaq-100 +2.2%, S&P +1.6%, Dow +1.3%; NVDA +3.6%, AMD +4.4%, AVGO +3.4%. Still on track for the worst November since 2008.

Bloomberg: Nvidia Blackwell racks found in a Shanghai data center tied to Alice Huang, founder of blacklisted Megaspeed. No Nvidia comment. Follows Thursday's halt of AI server shipments to four SE Asian countries.
10-year ~4.91% (+6.5 bp), 30-year ~5.29%; a December 9 hike ~99% priced; dollar index 103.80 (+0.1%).
Gold +3.8% to 3,698.50, silver +9.2% to 44.27, copper +4.2%; WTI +1.8% to 85.22 ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting (quota rollover talk).
Jefferies sees Brazil rebound potential after the finance minister pick; Brazilian ADRs catch up after the U.S. holiday (PBR +11.8%, ITUB +14%).
Goldman warns Friday's jump runs into a wave of automated selling (headline: $100 billion).

briefs.read: Risk-on into a half day: Nasdaq-100 futures +2.2% to +2.9%, S&P 500 +1.6% to +2.0%, Russell +1.45%, led by chips and neoclouds, with SPY and QQQ still under their 20-day averages after an ~8% Nasdaq-100 drop in November. VIX 25.3 (-5.6%). No red events; stocks close 1 p.m., bonds 2 p.m., so volume will be light. Wait for the first 15 minutes and be careful after about noon.

sentiment.read: Still Wednesday's 21 (from 11 on Nov 20, 28 Monday, 27 Tuesday). Bad news has stopped working on the AI names: Nvidia halted AI server shipments to four SE Asian countries Thursday and Bloomberg found Blackwell racks in Shanghai this morning, yet NVDA is +3.6% to +4.7% and AMD up to +7%, extending Wednesday's SPY recovery from -3.2% to -0.3%. Gold +3.8% and silver +9% rise with stocks while the 10-year yield climbs ~6 bp: this looks like short-covering and holiday re-entry, not one clean risk-on story. 49 days in 10 stretches is a small sample.
sentiment.positioned: Hedged and braced: VIX 25.3 even after a -5.6% drop, the fear curve 1.08 at Wednesday's close, chips -25.6% and high-growth -21.8% over a month while staples are +6.3%. The crowd is underweight chips and neoclouds, which is why they lead the bounce (CRWV +6.5-7.9%, NBIS +7-9.5%).
sentiment.surprise: If the 1 p.m. close holds the open, with SPY above 718.43 (Wednesday's high) and NVDA above 150.37, the braced crowd is caught short into the weekend. The other side: the open gets sold into the systematic selling Goldman flags and SPY slips under 712.14 (Tuesday's low) before the close, showing Friday was holiday short-covering.

bigPicture: Bad news has stopped pushing the AI names lower: the Nvidia shipment halt and the Blackwell-in-Shanghai report are being bought through, two sessions after SPY recovered from -3.2% on Wednesday.
The bounce is in the most-sold groups (chips -25.6%, high-growth -21.8% in a month): covering and holiday re-entry, not yet a trend change; every chip name is still well under its 20 and 50 EMAs.
Havens rise with stocks (gold, silver) while the 10-year climbs ~6 bp and a December hike stays ~99% priced: the rate backdrop has not eased.
Thin trading and a 1 p.m. close: Goldman warns of automated selling into the jump, so first-15-minute moves can reverse fast.
snapshot.takeaway: The most-sold AI names are bouncing through bad news, but it is a thin half day with a 1 p.m. close and systematic sellers waiting. Let the first 15 minutes settle and judge the bounce by whether NVDA and SPY hold their Wednesday highs (150.37 and 718.43).

briefs.read: Morning expected a thin risk-on bounce in chips that could reverse early; it did, then recovered. Gap fills paid first (NVDA to 145.39 at 9:45, AMD 398.59, CRWV 40.88); from 10:05 calls took over: MU +7.6%, AMD +4.6% over its opening high. SPY held 718.43, closed at its high 728.32 (+1.6%). Money into chips (SMH +4.2%), staples lagged. Monday: no red event; JOLTS 10 a.m.

sentiment.past: The last five years had this mood on 114 days in 18 separate stretches: the S&P 500 fund was higher five days later 51% of the time (middle result +0.0% after five days, +0.6% after ten).
sentiment.usual: On an ordinary day it was higher five days later 58% of the time.
sentiment.read: Mood jumped from 21 (extreme fear) to 34 in one half day; four of five readings now calm, only junk bonds still nervous. The open was sold (SPY 725.86 to 719.61 by 10:05, NVDA 151.94 to 145.39 by 9:45), but every dip was bought and the last ten minutes ran QQQ from ~646 to 651. Bad news (Nvidia shipment halt, Blackwell in Shanghai, S&P key-man review) did not push chips down: SMH +4.2%, MU +7.6%. VIX −11% while the 10-year rose to 4.93%: fear coming out, not rates easing.
sentiment.positioned: Less braced: fear curve back to 1.00, VIX under 24, the rush for protection is over. But 72% of big stocks are still under their 20-day average and chips sit far below their 20 and 50 EMAs, so most are still underweight the AI names; this looks like covering into a holiday weekend more than new money committing.
sentiment.surprise: The crowd now leans 'the bounce is on'. It would be caught out if Monday gives back Friday's late surge: SPY back under 718.43 (held all day, low 719.61), an OPEC+ surprise Sunday, or a hot JOLTS at 10 a.m. Monday pushing the 10-year over 5%. Other side: SPY holding above 728 with chips extending would say it was more than covering.
